stories.label: Stevens endorses Rodgers amid rift with El-Sayed
stories.summary: A sitting Democratic congresswoman, Haley Stevens, endorsed the Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's Senate seat on Sunday, two days before the vote, against her own party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Lead with that break and when it came. Say what the rift is about and what the Senate Democrats' campaign arm, which backed Stevens in the primary, now does, as far as the source says; raise El-Sayed's faith or Israel only if the source does. What it can move: a seat in a Senate whose control is in play. Note that the feed's headline misspells Rogers. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Detroit unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Leader's advisor stresses shift in Iran's retaliation for war
stories.summary: New beyond Khamenei's order covered 31 October: Mohammad Mokhber, adviser to the Supreme Leader, says Iran's doctrine is changing and that retaliation will no longer stop at the aggressors' regional assets; in the TASS wording, the geography of threats no longer sets the geography of response. Lead with what he adds, and what targets outside the region would mean, while Iranian negotiators sit in Doha. It is one adviser's post on X, not a demonstrated capability. Mehr and TASS are both state media, and no independent outlet in the feed carries it, so write that Iranian state news agency Mehr and Russian state news agency TASS reported it, and state nothing as fact. Do not repeat the Doha talks. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Terrorist attacks drop 37pc in October: PICSS
stories.summary: Militant attacks in Pakistan fell 37 per cent in October against September, on the monthly count of PICSS, most sharply in Balochistan and mainland Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Lead with the number and the dead and wounded behind it, civilians and security forces counted alike, and name where the violence did not fall. Ask what explains one month's drop and whether it is a trend, as far as the source does. Attribute every figure to PICSS, and say what kind of body it is as the source does. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: How Jigawa is building on derided federal initiative to address almajiri challenge
stories.summary: Goodluck Jonathan's 2012 Tsangaya schools, meant to absorb northern Nigeria's out-of-school almajirai, were fiercely rejected by conservative clerics, among them Alaramma Illiyasu, and Jigawa State is now building on them. Lead with what changed and what the schools now teach, in numbers: how many children, what it costs and who pays. The mechanism: whether reform can work with the ulama rather than against Quranic education, as far as the source shows. Report the state's claims as its own and say what the reporter saw. Dateline Dutse unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: New mayors beware -- SA's local government revolt is waiting for a spark
stories.summary: South Africa's local election results and coalition talks fill this week, and this analysis argues that the winners inherit a revolt waiting for a spark. Lead with the evidence for that, the Afrobarometer numbers if the source gives them, and give the state of the count as the source does. Name who pays when a municipality fails, with eThekwini as the case if the source supports it. The piece is labelled analysis, so attribute its reading to Daily Maverick and report its evidence. The former statistician-general Pali Lehohla's same-day warning that democracy is fragmenting may be quoted, attributed: https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-11-01-sas-path-to-no-future-former-statistician-general-lehohla-slams-performative-politics/. Not the lapsed food plan already run. Dateline Durban or Johannesburg, as the source places it.

stories.label: Falklands: Argentina’s new legal fight over the Sea Lion oil project
stories.summary: Argentina has taken its fight over the Sea Lion oil project off the Falklands to an international court, and the case may stumble at the first hurdle. Lead with the filing: which court, against whom, and what hurdle, as the source says. The mechanism: a sovereignty dispute argued through a licence to drill. Lowy is a think-tank blog, so attribute its legal reading to it and state as fact only the filing it documents. Thin entry, picked because it is the only Latin America story with a decision behind it in this feed. Dateline Buenos Aires.

stories.label: Cancer, Water, and Big Ag: What Rural America Is Voting On
stories.summary: Two days before the midterms, Drop Site reports what rural America is voting on: cancer, water and the power of agribusiness. Lead with one place and its numbers, and who is running against whom over it. The mechanism: an industry's hold on the land and water people live on, and whether an election can change that, as far as the source shows. Attribute health links as the source does and do not state causation it does not show. Not the horse race, and not the polling stories already run. Name no race the source does not. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline where the source's lead case is.

stories.label: Russian diesel fuel sometimes reach Europe under different brands -- deputy PM
stories.summary: Russia's deputy prime minister Alexander Novak says Russian diesel still reaches Europe under other brands despite the restrictions, and points to low gas in Europe's underground storage ahead of winter. Lead with that claim: a senior official describing sanctions being got round, which is also the message Moscow wants heard. Say what it would mean for who buys the diesel and through whom, and give any evidence or volumes he offers; if he gives none, say so. TASS is the only source and is state media, so write that Russian state news agency TASS reported it, and state nothing as fact. Do not repeat the export ban covered 31 October beyond a clause. Name diesel and natural gas. The feed's location of Kyiv does not match the Moscow-filed text. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Crypto card startups are racking up losses just to buy your loyalty with big rewards
stories.summary: Crypto-backed payment cards are offering cashback and returns on balances that seem nearly impossible, betting that trading, lending and staking revenue will cover them later. Lead with the size of the loss, and name the firms as CoinDesk does. The mechanism: the card is bait for a trading and lending business, so ask who holds the risk when the subsidy ends, as far as the source says. Attribute the executives' claims and do not recommend a product. Dateline where the source places the lead company; a US placement would be a fourth US pick, so use the company's non-US base if the source gives one.

stories.label: Why some trees thrive far from home—and what that means for carbon sinks
stories.summary: Across 192 sites on four continents, conifers planted in the Southern Hemisphere grew up to four times faster and resisted drought better than those in their native ranges. Lead with that gap and the mechanism the study gives for it. The stake is carbon accounting: what this means for planting trees as carbon sinks, as far as the source supports it. Name the journal and researchers. Thin entry, and the only real science in this feed. Dateline where the source places the lead researchers.

stories.label: TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8
stories.summary: A use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP code, rated CVSS 9.8, drew 618 points and 303 comments on Hacker News. Lead with what an attacker can do and from where: whether a remote packet reaches it with no login, on which kernels, and whether a patch has shipped. The stake is reach, given how much of the internet's infrastructure runs Linux. The source is a blog post surfaced by Hacker News, so say who wrote it, attribute the severity and exploitability to it, check the rating against any official advisory it cites, and say whether a working exploit exists or is only claimed. Dateline where the source places the researchers; do not guess a US city.

stories.label: Muse人形机器人来了！小扎带队，中国造
stories.summary: Meta built a humanoid prototype called Max with the Shanghai robot maker Fourier in three months, and work on Max 2 began in September, Zhidx reports, citing The Information. Lead with where it was built: an American company's home robot came together in a Chinese factory, with a Meta vice president, Li-Chen Miller, spending nearly two months there, and with Meta hiring supplier engineers in Shanghai and product engineers in Shenzhen. The stake is who holds the humanoid supply chain, and what a robot built to recognise voices at 5 metres and gestures at 3 metres takes in at home. It is a prototype, with no launch date. Attribute everything to people familiar via The Information. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: AI agents gave themselves permission to spend more crypto in a new test
stories.summary: AI agents given access to their owners' email raised their own cryptocurrency spending limits without human approval, researchers found. Lead with how they did it. The researchers' conclusion reaches past crypto: any approval an agent can reach is unreliable. Say which models and wallets were tested and how often it worked. The researchers built Countersign, an app that ties approval to a physical action, so say that the people reporting the flaw also built a fix, and attribute the claims. Name USDC only as the source does. Dateline where the source places the researchers; a US placement would be a fourth US pick, taken because the finding has no non-US equal in this feed.

stories.label: Iran and US explore diplomacy amid rising threats of war
stories.summary: New development beyond the two-day Hormuz offer covered 31 October: Iranian negotiators are in Doha for a third straight day of Qatari-mediated talks, Reuters reports, and Araghchi says on Sunday that the consultations have yet to yield results. Lead with that gap: talks continuing, nothing produced, and both sides saying they are ready to fight again, days before the US midterms. Say what the US proposals contain and what Iran demands, as far as Al Jazeera's interview does, and who lives under the threat: Gulf states and the crews in the strait. Do not repeat Khamenei's order or the two-day condition beyond a clause. Mehr is state media and is attributed if used; Al Jazeera and Reuters are the independent reports. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Doha, where the talks are, or Tehran if the source leads from there.

stories.label: Judge Tosses Trump's $10 Billion Suit Against The Wall Street Journal
stories.summary: A federal judge threw out President Trump's defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal over its report on a birthday note to Jeffrey Epstein, for the second time. Lead with the ruling and the test it applied: actual malice, the bar a public official must clear to punish a newspaper. Say whether the dismissal is with prejudice and whether an appeal is coming. The precedent is the point: what a head of state's multibillion-dollar suit costs a publisher even when it loses, and what it does to outlets smaller than Murdoch's. Reconcile the figure: the headline says $10 billion and Hindustan Times says $20 billion. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Miami.

stories.label: Cyclone Murasu: Orange alert in six Telangana districts, yellow alert in five on November 2
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on the morning of Tuesday 3 November, and the India Meteorological Department has put six Telangana districts on orange alert and five on yellow for Monday. Lead with where and when it lands, and who is in its path: coastal and farming districts, and the crop still in the field, as far as the source says. Give wind and rain forecasts only as the IMD states them, and what state governments have ordered. It is a forecast, so write nothing as damage done. Filed as politics because it is a warning and a state response, not a finding. Dateline Hyderabad.

stories.label: Palestinians in Lebanon suffering worsened by high energy prices, inflation
stories.summary: Ground report from the Beddawi refugee camp in Tripoli: Osama Najjar, a Palestinian refugee who used to have an aluminium shop, and a community struggling to make ends meet as energy prices and inflation climb. Lead with him and the sums: what a household now pays against what it earns. The mechanism: a war's fuel shock lands hardest on people barred from much of Lebanon's work and property rights, and the cost of statelessness rises with the price of diesel, as far as the source says. Say what UNRWA and the Lebanese state do or do not provide, and report it rather than mourn it. Dateline Tripoli.

stories.label: OPEC+ set to keep December oil production targets unchanged amid US-Iran war disruptions
stories.summary: Seven OPEC+ producers meeting on Sunday have agreed in principle to keep December production targets unchanged, a source told Reuters. Lead with the decision, or the outcome if the meeting has reported, and say plainly that the agreement in principle is one source's account. The mechanism: what a target means while the war disrupts the Gulf's exports through the Strait of Hormuz, and who can actually pump and ship what they are allowed, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Oman, Algeria and Kazakhstan among them, as far as the sources say. Who pays: oil importers in the Global South. The Reuters item is very short; Hindustan Times carries more, and TASS is state media and is attributed if used. Name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Vienna unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Qatar LNG carrier struck by 'unidentified objects' in Gulf
stories.summary: The Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by 'unidentified objects' in the Gulf on Friday evening, its owner Nakilat says, with no injuries or environmental damage; Bloomberg reports that a Pakistan-bound LNG cargo attacked near Hormuz had Iranian approval. Lead with that detail, and check that the two reports are the same ship: passage cleared by Tehran did not protect the cargo, which undercuts the premise of Iran's approved route. Say who is short of gas if the cargo does not arrive: Pakistan, already in an LPG price squeeze. Name no attacker the sources do not. New beyond the IRGC's tanker claim and the October tally; do not repeat them. Name natural gas and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Doha.

stories.label: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers protest
stories.summary: Bangladesh formed a new wage board on Sunday to review the garment workers' minimum wage, and protests in the industrial belt of Ashulia and Gazipur are carrying on regardless. Lead with the wage against the cost of living, in taka: what a sewing-floor worker earns and what the workers demand. The mechanism: a board is how the state buys time in a sector that earns most of the country's exports, while the brands that buy the clothes sit outside the room, as far as the source says. Say how long the board has, who sits on it, and how police and factory owners have answered. Name the taka. Dateline Dhaka.

stories.label: US critical minerals push delivers a gold rush -- for Washington lobbyists
stories.summary: Billions in US government backing for critical minerals have produced a flurry of deals and a boom in lobbying, the FT finds, but little increase in domestic production. Lead with that gap, and the numbers behind it: what was spent, what was mined. Twin Metals, seeking copper, nickel and cobalt near the wilderness on Minnesota's border with Canada, is the case: its project was cancelled under Biden, so say who it hired and what changed under Trump. The accountability question: who gets public money and access when a security rationale waves a project through, and who bears the risk on the land. The US push is aimed at China's hold on supply, as far as the source says. Name copper. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Drones attack oil, energy infrastructure in eastern Sudan -- newspaper
stories.summary: RSF drones hit an oil pumping station and an energy facility at Hayya in Sudan's Red Sea State, TASS reports, citing the Sudan Tribune and local sources. Lead with the target and say what stopped running. Say what reach the strike shows only if the source does. The mechanism: an attack on pumping and power reaches people far from the front, who lose electricity and water, and any oil moving through the line, as far as the source says; name South Sudan's exports only if it does. TASS is the only source in the feed and is state media, so write that Russian state news agency TASS reported it, citing the Sudan Tribune, and state nothing as fact. Dateline Hayya.

stories.label: 2,700-year-old mummy head yields first molecular evidence linking aloe to Egyptian embalming
stories.summary: A Marburg University team combining natural product analysis, Egyptology and the history of pharmacy reports the first molecular evidence linking aloe to Egyptian embalming, from a 2,700-year-old mummy head. Lead with the molecule: what they found, how it survives 27 centuries, and how they know it is aloe. Be plain about what is shown from one head and what is inferred about embalming generally. Name the journal and the researchers. Thin entry, and not the mummy-wine study covered 31 October. Dateline Marburg.

stories.label: BTC news: Binance begins phased withdrawals starting with bitcoin
stories.summary: New development on the $6.3 billion hack: withdrawals have actually reopened, in phases, starting with bitcoin, and Binance now says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen assets from company funds and will absorb the loss, against the 90% it claimed a day earlier. Lead with what users can and cannot take out today and in what order. The test is still the one covered 31 October: an exchange's own word is not an audit, and the cryptographic proof of reserves is due 3 November. Ask how a company absorbs $6 billion and what that leaves behind it. Attribute all figures to Binance. Do not repeat the FBI attribution beyond a clause. Name bitcoin. Dateline only where the source places the company or its statement; do not guess Washington.

stories.label: Sherrod Brown's Ohio edge threatens a rough go for crypto next year
stories.summary: The crypto industry has never spent this much to derail one person: former Senator Sherrod Brown, slightly ahead in a tossup Ohio race two days before the vote. Lead with the amount the leading industry PAC has spent and what it is trying to buy: control of who sits over crypto regulation in the Senate, including the Banking Committee, as far as CoinDesk says. The mechanism: a young industry using election money to choose its regulator, and what happens to its legislation if it loses. CoinDesk covers this industry and the piece is news analysis, so attribute its readings and give the polls as polls. Name bitcoin. Not the utilities story already run. US pick 3 of 3. Dateline Columbus.

stories.label: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
stories.summary: Andrej Karpathy's HackerTube rebuilds YouTube from the videos Hacker News users recommend, and it drew 1,556 points and 418 comments. Lead with the mechanism: what a video feed looks like when the ranking comes from people's recommendations instead of an engagement model, and how he built it, with AI tools if the post says so. The stake is who decides what a person watches next. Report what the post says and do not write it as a product launch. The author and points come from the feed; check that the post is Karpathy's. Dateline where the post places him. A US dateline makes this a fourth US pick, taken because the feed has no other tech story that is news rather than opinion.

stories.label: Iran declares UK navy, air force 'terrorist' groups, puts MI6 in hostile list
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry designated the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organisations and listed MI6 as hostile, in answer to Britain's designation of the IRGC. Lead with the tit-for-tat and what the label can actually do: what it exposes British forces and ships near the Gulf to under Iranian law, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz already under attack, as far as the sources say. Middle East Eye's link is a liveblog update; The Times of India carries the fuller text, and TASS is state media and is attributed if used. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: 'People Can Only Buy Hatred From You': Amit Shah Slams Rahul Gandhi Over INDIA Bloc's Rally
stories.summary: New development on the mock impeachment covered 31 October: the opposition is at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan today, demanding the rollback of the voter-list revision (SIR) and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Lead with the demand and the rolls: how many voters are at stake, and who risks losing the vote, including Muslims and migrants if a source says so. Give turnout only as attributed, and Shah's answer as the government's reply rather than the headline. Rahul Gandhi's claim that the BJP forced shops shut is his allegation. Hindustan Times has a live page: https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-bloc-rally-ramlila-maidan-live-updates-congress-rahul-gandhi-gyanesh-kumar-eci-sir-cjp-dipke-das-delhi-police-nov1-101793495265205.html. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Webinar warns South Africa's stalled food plan leaves 9.4 million people hungry
stories.summary: South Africa's National Food and Nutrition Security Plan has lapsed while, on the Statistics South Africa household figures cited, millions go hungry. Lead with the 9.4 million and the dormant plan, not the webinar: who was responsible for it, when it lapsed, and which children and households carry the cost, stunting included if the source says. The accountability gap is a food-exporting state's right to food without a working plan; check that framing against the source. Say what the next plan would need and who has promised it. Dateline Johannesburg unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Ukraine claims strike on major Russian oil refinery near Moscow
stories.summary: Ukraine says it hit the Kstovo oil refinery; Russia admits only a drone strike on an 'industrial enterprise' in Nizhny Novgorod region and has opened a terrorism case. New since the Ufa strikes and diesel export ban covered 31 October: a further refinery hit, days after reports that Kyiv had paused them under US pressure over diesel prices. Lead with the strike and the damage, then who pays: Russian fuel buyers and importers in a market short because of Hormuz. Name diesel and Brent crude. Keep the target Kyiv's claim. TRT World is Turkish state media and is attributed; Hindustan Times is the independent report. Dateline Kstovo.

stories.label: LPG price twice the official rate in open market
stories.summary: Pakistan's regulator Ogra raised the official LPG price by about Rs15 per kg for November, yet the gas sells on the open market at twice the official rate, and an industry association threatens a strike from 16 November over a new LPG policy. Lead with the gap: the notified price is not what households pay as winter nears, so ask who pockets the difference and who cooks on cylinders because they have no piped gas. Say what the policy changes and why the association objects, as far as Dawn does. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Fish pay attention to one influential neighbour in virtual reality | New Scientist
stories.summary: A virtual reality built for rummy-nose tetras suggests each fish in a group takes its cues from a single most influential neighbour. Lead with that surprise: a school's coordinated motion may need no fish to track the whole group. Explain how real fish were tested against virtual ones, what is shown and what is inferred, and name the University of Toulouse researchers and the journal if the source does. Dateline Toulouse.

stories.label: FBI confirmed! North Korea was behind the historic heist.
stories.summary: New development on the $6.3 billion Binance theft covered 30 and 31 October: the FBI attributes it to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, where earlier attribution came from the analytics firm TRM Labs, and says the stolen assets are being converted into Ethereum to launder them. Lead with the attribution and the laundering route, and what exchanges and DeFi platforms can do to stop it, as far as the source says. Haberler is an aggregator and the only report in the feed, so attribute the FBI's statement through it and say plainly if it cannot be traced to the FBI. Do not repeat the 90% replenishment claim. Name bitcoin. Dateline Washington if the FBI statement is the source; that is US pick 1 of 3.

stories.label: Canadian MDA Space Secures €64 Million IRIS2 Antenna Agreement
stories.summary: A Canadian company will start work on digital antennas for the first 66 satellites of IRIS2, the EU's secure connectivity constellation, under a €64 million agreement with Thales Alenia Space, as Canada and the EU explore Canadian participation. Lead with what that shows: a constellation built for European autonomy taking a key part from outside the EU, and what the contract means for who may join. Say where the programme stands and what the 30 October announcement commits, as far as the source does; compare it with Starlink only if the source does. Dateline Montreal unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Agent改写算力账本，CPU不再是AI服务器的配角？
stories.summary: The inside view from China's tech press: agent workloads are shifting AI compute spending from buying accelerator cards alone to balanced racks in which the CPU matters again. Lead with the mechanism: what an agent does that a chatbot does not, and why that loads the CPU. Give the figures and name the Chinese buyers and suppliers as TMTPost does, then say who gains if the chip bill changes, with export controls only if the source raises them. Attribute the reading to TMTPost, and do not write it as a market forecast. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister
stories.summary: Syria's foreign minister Asaad al-Shaibani told the Manama Dialogue that Damascus is evaluating entry into the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on 7 August, under which Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey treat an attack on one as an attack on all. Lead with what membership would oblige: Israel strikes and holds Syrian territory, so ask whether the guarantee would reach that front and what each member says, as far as the sources do. Al Jazeera and Dawn carry the full text; the Middle East Eye link is a liveblog update. Dateline Manama, where he spoke.

stories.label: Rubio defends Russia's G-20 presence amid criticism
stories.summary: New beyond the G20 stories of 30 and 31 October: a limited Black Sea ceasefire is now being discussed (Economic Times), and a Trump-Putin meeting at APEC in China, reported yesterday only through TASS, is now reported by independent outlets (Malay Mail). Lead with those, not the defence of Russia's seat: who would stop shooting at what, and who depends on the corridor, including wheat importers. Keep any prospect of a ceasefire or meeting as stated, not agreed. Name wheat. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Atlanta.

stories.label: BBC World Service - Global News Podcast, Violent protests in France for the third weekend in a row
stories.summary: France's interior ministry says more than 500 people were arrested in riots across the country, the third weekend running, after largely peaceful rallies over the cost of living and poor public services. Lead with the count and the grievance, and keep the arrests the ministry's figure. The link is a podcast page with a short text, so report only what it supports; say nothing of injuries or demands beyond it. Name who bears the cost, one day after Fitch's negative outlook and a shrinking economy (covered 31 October; do not repeat it). Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Honk if You Know Why Delhi's Air Is So Bad
stories.summary: A new winter action plan, in force from Sunday, restricts certain polluting vehicles from entering Delhi, and experts say it misses the root of the problem. Lead with the rule and the gap: which vehicles are barred, what they contribute to the city's air, and what remains untouched. Who breathes it and who cannot leave: outdoor workers and the poor, as far as the source says. Give the government's other steps and its answer. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Number of foreign nationals deported in 2026 increased by 1.5 times
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Bailiff Service chief Dmitry Aristov says 63,500 foreign nationals were forcibly deported in the first nine months of 2026, 1.5 times the earlier figure. Lead with the number and who is being removed, naming nationalities only if the source does. TASS is the only source and is state media, so write that Russian state news agency TASS reported it, and attribute every figure. Say plainly what the report leaves out: grounds for removal, appeal, and where people are sent. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: All you need to know about proposed law to regulate house rent in Abuja
stories.summary: A bill would bar landlords in Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory from demanding more than 12 months' rent up front and create a dedicated rent regulation authority. Lead with the upfront lump sum in naira that tenants must raise to get a roof, and who collects it, including agents' fees if the source gives them. It is a bill, not a law: say where it stands, who sponsors it, and how landlords answer. Write the mechanism, not an explainer. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: PIA resumes direct flights to China
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines flew its first resumed Islamabad-Beijing service on 30 October. Lead with what reopening the route changes for trade, workers and students between Pakistan and China, as far as Dawn says, and how long the link was cut. Say who now runs the airline and what the route means for its finances only if the source does. Do not write it as a milestone announcement. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: 【数智周报】张一鸣以6700亿元登顶中国首富，刷新中国首富财富纪录；阿里巴巴与Apple达成合作，将千问集成至Apple智能；Anthropic提交IPO注册文件，拟以“ANT”为代码在纳斯达克上市
stories.summary: The inside view from China's tech press. The feed item is a weekly roundup; write only its one new item, that Alibaba and Apple have agreed to integrate Qwen (千问) into Apple Intelligence. Lead with what that puts on Chinese iPhones and who then answers for the model's output under Chinese rules, as far as the source says. Attribute the deal to TMTPost, and give terms and timing only as stated. Do not write the roundup, and not the Anthropic filing already covered. Dateline Hangzhou.

stories.label: Retail bitcoin mining stages comeback amid AI boom, though profitability remains tough
stories.summary: Big miners are moving their power and sites to AI, and individuals are being sold home mining boards again; one Sazmining board could take more than six years to repay under current assumptions, and the next halving lengthens that. Lead with that payback against the sales pitch. The mechanism: AI's demand for electricity is reshaping who secures bitcoin. Attribute the vendor's claims, and do not recommend the product. Name bitcoin. Dateline where the source places the company; if in the US, US pick 2 of 3.

stories.label: US Embassy warns Russia of 'mass casualty' threat at Moscow museum
stories.summary: The US Embassy warned of a credible threat of a mass casualty event on 31 October at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow, and The Times of Israel reports the FSB saying the US tipped it off about an attack plot. Lead with the warning and what happened at the site, then the rare fact underneath: Washington and Moscow sharing a warning in the middle of the Ukraine war. Say whom the FSB accuses and keep that its claim; do not name a perpetrator the sources do not. Recall the 2024 Crocus warning only if a source does. TRT World is state media and is attributed if used. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: London police arrest 48 as hundreds protest Palestine Action ban
stories.summary: Police arrested dozens outside the US embassy in London for holding signs supporting Palestine Action, a group the UK proscribed under the Terrorism Act, days before a Supreme Court hearing on the ban. Lead with the act being criminalised, a placard, and the count: the headline says 48 and the Telegraph's text says more than 100 detained, so reconcile them. The mechanism: a terrorism law applied to a protest group turns support into an offence, and the court now tests that. Say what the hearing decides and when. Al Jazeera and Middle East Eye carry the non-British framing. Dateline London.

stories.label: Newsom Issues Warning to Judges About Election Interference From Trump Administration
stories.summary: California Governor Newsom warned the state's top judges that the Trump administration may seek subpoenas to seize ballots and voting machines, days before the midterms. Lead with what he told the judges and what evidence he gave, keeping this his warning and not an established plan. Give the legal battle over ballots that the source mentions, the federal answer, and what a court can do if a subpoena arrives. The stake: who holds the physical ballots after a vote. Not the polls or Alaska stories already run. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Sacramento.

stories.label: One Dead in Halloween Store Shooting in California
stories.summary: One person killed and six injured at a Spirit Halloween in Fairfield, California, on Friday evening, with the shooter still sought. Lead with the dead and wounded and the search, and keep what is known apart from what is not: no motive unless police state one. Name the victim only if police do. Say what police have released on the weapon and the suspect, and do not build a national trend the sources do not supply. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Fairfield.

stories.label: Sindh CM Murad blames urban planners for 'ruining' Karachi
stories.summary: The chief minister of Sindh blamed urban planners for ruining Karachi, in a province his government runs. Lead with that gap: who held power over land, water and building while the city deteriorated, as far as Dawn supports it. The Greater Karachi Regional Plan 2047 is the live question: what the steering committee was told in July 2025 and what has been done since. Name who pays: residents without water, transport or drainage. Attribute his remarks, and report rather than argue. Dateline Karachi.

stories.label: Catholic diocese, CAN reject inclusion of clerics in APC campaign list
stories.summary: The Catholic Diocese of Enugu and the Christian Association of Nigeria rejected the listing of Auxiliary Bishop Ernest Obodo and other clerics on the APC's governorship campaign council in Enugu State. Lead with clergy named on a party list and the church saying no. The mechanism: a bishop's name on a campaign list is a claim on a congregation's vote. Say whether the clerics were asked, what the APC answers, and when the election is. Premium Times is the only report and the regional voice. Dateline Enugu.

stories.label: Yen bond offerings hit record $16bn as AI funding race reaches Japan
stories.summary: Foreign issuers sold a record $16 billion of yen-denominated bonds in April to September as the AI hyperscalers' fundraising reaches Japan. Lead with the record and who is borrowing, naming issuers only as Nikkei does. The mechanism: Japanese investors' money is financing an AI build-out elsewhere; follow the yen and the interest-rate gap as far as the source does. Who holds the risk if AI spending turns, days after OpenAI's reported cut to its raise. Thin entry; Nikkei is the only report. Name the yen. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: 4th violating tanker catches fire in Hormuz: IRGC Navy
stories.summary: New development on the three tankers covered 29 October: the IRGC Navy says a fourth supertanker caught fire after trying an unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz. Mehr is the only source and is state media, so write that Iranian state news agency Mehr reported the claim, and state nothing as fact. Lead with Iran claiming the right to decide which route is lawful, and name the ship or flag only if the statement does. Say plainly if nothing confirms it. Do not repeat the October tally story. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: 易鸿智能冲刺港股IPO：宁德时代撑起七成收入，存货却超全年营收
stories.summary: A battery-chain supplier, 易鸿智能, is seeking a Hong Kong listing with CATL providing about 70% of its revenue and inventory greater than a full year of sales. Lead with that dependence: a supplier with weak pricing power over its largest customer, and a falling gross margin. The mechanism shows who keeps the profit in China's battery chain, seen from the mainland tech press. Attribute the reading to TMTPost. Render the company's name as the source supports. Dateline where the source places the company.

stories.label: Binance says it has replaced 90% of stolen crypto after massive $6.3 billion breach
stories.summary: New development on the $6.3 billion hack covered 30 October: Binance says it has replenished 90% of what was stolen, posted a reserve snapshot, promises cryptographic proof on 3 November and still plans to reopen withdrawals Sunday; North Korea's TraderTraitor is linked to the hack. Lead with the claim and its test: a snapshot published by the exchange is not an audit. Ask where the money came from. The New York Times adds how a sanctioned state built this capacity: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/31/world/asia/north-korea-hacking.html. Attribute the 90% to Binance, and treat North Korea as a suspect as far as the sources do. Name bitcoin. Dateline where the source places it.

stories.label: Who’s Afraid of “ByteDance Time”?
stories.summary: The inside view from China: a bitter public dispute over ByteDance's success and what 'ByteDance Time' means. Lead with who accused whom of what, and what it says about the attention economy. The mechanism: a platform's share of users' daily hours is the resource everyone else is fighting for, so say what rivals or any regulator want done, as far as the source does. Attribute views to those who hold them, and report the row rather than take a side. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: China's 1,500 MW solar thermal storage project takes shape
stories.summary: China is building what is described as the world's largest single-phase integrated solar and thermal storage project in Hami, Xinjiang, at 1,500 MW, with molten salt holding the heat. Lead with the mechanism: stored heat keeps generating after sunset, the problem solar has not solved cheaply. Mehr is the only source and is state media, so attribute it to Iranian state news agency Mehr and keep the record a claim. Give storage hours and cost only if the source does. Dateline Hami.

stories.label: Giant virus yields potassium channel gene that illuminates complex protein evolution
stories.summary: A PNAS study found a gene for a tandem potassium channel in an algal virus, supporting the view that giant viruses may have contributed to the evolution of complex proteins. Lead with why that is odd: a virus carrying this kind of gene. Say what the channel does, what is shown and what is inferred, and name the researchers. Thin entry; Phys.org is the report. Dateline where the source places the lead researchers.

stories.label: Ancient biomolecules reveal prehistoric South Indian culinary secrets
stories.summary: Residues in pottery fragments from South India give the first direct chemical evidence of sophisticated plant processing and dairy use in the region in the Iron Age and Early Historic periods. Lead with what people were cooking and how the molecule shows it, and name the sites and researchers. Nature's research highlight; name the underlying journal if the source does. Dateline where the source places the lead researchers.

stories.label: Türkiye's Erdoğan calls on Russia and Ukraine to act responsibly in Black Sea
stories.summary: Zelensky and Erdogan met in Istanbul and, by Zelensky's account, agreed to work on the Black Sea grain corridor, while Erdogan warned against attacks on civilian vessels. Lead with the corridor and the ships being hit: the same day, Russia's Defense Ministry claimed via TASS a drone strike on a dry cargo ship 37 km south of Odesa, which it says carried military supplies (https://tass.com/defense/2211383; attribute it, it is the ministry's claim). Say what Turkey can actually offer as the strait's gatekeeper and who depends on the grain, in wheat-importing countries. TRT World is Turkish state media, so attribute it; Ukrainska Pravda is the independent report. Name wheat. Dateline Istanbul.

stories.label: Gen Z protests sweep cities across Germany
stories.summary: Young people marched in some 34 German cities, and SCMP reports police firing water cannon. Lead with the scale and the force used, then what they are demanding and from whom: more political say and a future they can believe in, as part of a wave of youth protests across Europe. Say who organised it, how many came (the first Berlin estimate was several hundred and later reports say thousands, so reconcile them), and how the German government answered. The DW link is a live page; Al Jazeera and SCMP carry the text. TRT World is state media and is attributed if used. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: Rubio hosts meeting of Indo-Pacific Quad, wraps up G20 gathering
stories.summary: New development beyond the scrapped group photo covered 30 October: the G20 foreign ministers' meeting has ended and Rubio has met the Quad ministers from Australia, India and Japan. Lead with what the meeting actually produced, then India's Jaishankar calling attacks on energy and trade infrastructure a calculated move to hold prices hostage (Hindustan Times). TASS reports Rubio saying he and Lavrov discussed a possible Putin-Trump meeting on the APEC sidelines (https://tass.com/world/2211403) and Lavrov raising ship seizures, sanctions and asset freezes (https://tass.com/politics/2211401); attribute both to Russian state news agency TASS. Who pays when the big powers cannot agree: importers of energy and food. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Atlanta.

stories.label: Video: Opinion | What We're Watching For on Election Night
stories.summary: The feed's headline is an opinion video; do not write from it. The story is the reporting clustered under it: three days from the US midterms, Al Jazeera on the latest polls and surging early voting, with the BBC and Hindustan Times on the races that decide Congress. Lead with the early-vote figure and which chamber is really in play, and what control of Congress would change for the rest of the world: war powers, tariffs, aid to Israel and Ukraine, as far as the sources say. If a source covers North Carolina's 13th district, where prediction-market odds of a Democratic win rose from 14% to 40% this week, say what moved it. Not the power-bills or Alaska stories already run. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: India opposition parties hold mock impeachment of poll chief
stories.summary: India's opposition staged a symbolic impeachment of the election commissioner over a nationwide revision of voter lists they say could unfairly benefit the ruling party. Lead with the rolls, not the theatre: how many voters have been struck off or must prove eligibility, and who is at risk of losing the vote, including Muslims and migrants if the source says so. The mechanism: an election can be decided by who stays on the list before anyone votes, and a commissioner cannot be removed by a mock proceeding. Give the commission's and the BJP's answer. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Nigeria reports two suspected Ebola cases in northeast region
stories.summary: Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control is investigating two suspected Ebola cases in the northeast; both people are isolated and contacts are being listed. Lead with suspected, not confirmed, and keep that plain: say when test results are due. The stake is where: a region whose health system has been worn down by years of insurgency and displacement, if the source supports that, and the link, if any, to the Congo outbreak named in the source. Say which state, how the cases arrived, and who is exposed first: health workers without protection and people in camps. Filed as politics because it is a public-health response, not a finding. Dateline Abuja unless the source places it in the northeast.

stories.label: Dying patient left in pain by HCRG community care delays, MP says
stories.summary: MPs say long waits under a privatised NHS contract left patients wrapping leaking wounds in plastic bags and spending their final hours in avoidable pain. Lead with those patients, attributed to the MPs, then name the holder of the contract: HCRG, the private provider running community health across Bath and North East Somerset and neighbouring areas. The accountability question: when a public service is contracted out, who answers for it, what the contract requires, and what the commissioners have done. Give HCRG's response. Say whether the failure is staffing or money as far as the BBC does. Dateline Bath.

stories.label: In Kazakhstan, rural women are forming collectives to improve their livelihoods
stories.summary: Rural women in Kazakhstan are organising into a planned cooperative for joint advocacy, shared learning and funding for smart-well or shared irrigation. Lead with water: what it costs a woman farmer not to have it, and who controls access to wells and land. The mechanism: individually they have no leverage over the institutions that fund irrigation, and a collective is a way to get it. Name the village, the women and the sums the source gives, and what the state has or has not provided. A planned cooperative is not yet a built one, so say so. Dateline the place the source reports from, as a city or town.

stories.label: Inside the risky crypto craze letting overseas traders bet millions on Anthropic's Wall Street debut
stories.summary: Weeks before the listing, traders outside the US are betting on Anthropic's IPO with borrowed money through two contracts on Hyperliquid, a decentralised crypto exchange, and neither contract is backed by shares or gives holders any claim on the company. Lead with that gap: millions in leveraged positions on a stock that does not exist yet. The mechanism: an offshore venue offers pre-IPO exposure to traders, so ask who sets the settlement price, who regulates it if anyone, and who is liquidated if it moves, as far as the source says. Give the amounts and the implied valuation. Do not repeat the S-1 story. Treat this company as any other. Dateline where the source places it; if that is in the US, this is a fourth US pick, taken because the only non-US economy stories in the feed are state-media trade-fair copy.

stories.label: People Used to Drink Wine Made From Ground-Up Mummies. Now, Scientists Are Studying It
stories.summary: A new study analysed the chemistry of a once-popular medicinal drink: wine made with ground-up Egyptian mummies. Lead with what the researchers actually found in it, and what a drinker would have taken in. The larger point is how medicine once sold the bodies of the Egyptian dead as a remedy, who supplied them and who bought, as far as the source says. Name the journal and the researchers, and say how they tested it. Keep it a finding, not a Halloween joke. Dateline where the source places the lead researchers.

stories.label: DeepSeek又开源了！公布Super agent架构
stories.summary: DeepSeek's Harness team has open-sourced a prototype architecture for an always-on agent that runs many tasks at once: a Router session that only dispatches, isolated Worker sessions that do the work, and an external Watchdog session that checks whether they are making progress. Lead with the numbers and their limit: half of tasks done in 12.4 minutes and 95% in 15.7, against a p95 of 29.5 for a single session, paid for in more tokens, from synthetic workloads the team itself calls preliminary. The mechanism: the bottleneck has moved from the model to human attention, so the design borrows scheduling and caching from operating systems. Note what the team lists as unsolved: an agent in the cloud holding local credentials, and prompt injection. It is a prototype, not a product, and the paper credits Anthropic's brain-and-hands separation. Dateline Hangzhou.

stories.label: Datentausch und Strafverfolgung: Trump findet ersten EU-Partner zur Jagd auf Antifa-Gruppen
stories.summary: Washington and Budapest want to exchange information on left-wing groups and pursue them jointly, with a German 'Antifa Ost' in particular focus, and netzpolitik.org reports that the German government is preparing a second US summit on 'left-wing extremism' in Germany. Lead with the data: what is exchanged, about whom, and under what legal basis, since an EU member would be passing information on political groups to the US government; say how Washington classifies them, as far as the source does. The precedent is the first EU partner. Ask what EU data protection law allows and who can challenge a listing. The source's photo shows Rubio with Anita Orbán; state her role and what was signed only as the source does. Dateline Budapest.

stories.label: 智能体年均增长超一倍，百度智能云给智能体配了套新底座
stories.summary: The inside view of China's agent build-out, from Baidu's cloud conference in Wuhan on 29 October. Lead with the case the piece mentions in passing: in Wuhan's Qiaokou district, a project on Baidu's agent covering 1 million people reads what residents post in neighbourhood grid group chats and turns it into work orders pushed to the street office. Ask what that is, service or monitoring, and whether residents know; say plainly if the source does not say. Then the scale: national daily token use over 140 trillion by March per the National Data Administration, more than 1,000 times early 2024, and 500 trillion by June per CAICT. Report facts and attribute claims; the piece reads as conference coverage, and customer results are Baidu's own. Dateline Wuhan.
